concept.name: Playbook
concept.definition: A trader's curated, documented collection of proven setups - each with context conditions, entry, exit, sizing, and a worked example - built from personal trading results and reviewed regularly. Popularized by Mike Bellafiore (One Good Trade; The PlayBook), it turns scattered experience into an explicit library of tradable patterns.
concept.intuition: Instead of trading everything the market shows you, you trade only the handful of patterns you have written down, tested, and own.
concept.mechanics: Each playbook entry documents one setup: market context, trigger, invalidation, targets, sizing rule, and annotated screenshots from real trades; entries are added from review of one's own best trades and retired when tracked expectancy decays. Setup-quality grading (A/B/C) is applied against playbook definitions.
concept.failure_modes: Playbooks ossify: setups fitted to one market regime keep being traded after the regime ends, so each entry needs ongoing expectancy tracking. Copying another trader's playbook without one's own screen time and data usually fails.
concept.misconceptions: A playbook is not a list of chart patterns from a book; it is a personal, evidence-backed subset of what that trader executes best. More setups is not better - depth in a few beats breadth.
concept.example: A trader's playbook holds four setups; when his quarterly review shows one has been negative for 60 trades, it is retired and replaced by a pattern his journal shows emerging.
